inputs.text: President John Mahama has stressed that the foundational policies of the nation are tied to its legal frameworks, cultural ethos, and collective societal agreement. He is emphasizing his dedication to upholding the rule of law amid these complex global human rights discussions. The social justice advocates are twisting this into a demand for institutional reforms to dismantle historical inequalities, prioritize labor rights, and attack cultural norms. That is the wrong path. This should instead reinforce our commitment to traditional authority, national sovereignty, family values, and personal responsibility, rather than allowing progressive agendas to erode social order and cultural continuity.
